title: Unary Index Run
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $r,u$ be binary words. Suppose a binary input $x$ is the concatenation of a prefix $p$ and the self-delimiting encoding of the word $1^k r$ paired with $u$. From the configuration whose state is the unary-index evaluation state with accumulator $c$, whose input head has consumed $|p|$ bits, whose work tape contains $u$, and whose work head is at integer position $h$, the verifier reaches after exactly $2k$ steps the configuration in the same state, with $|p|+2k$ input bits consumed, the same work tape, and work head at $h+k$.
hypotheses_covered: $x=p$ concatenated with the pair encoding of $1^k r$ and $u$
the initial input position is valid as witnessed by the stated length bound
initial state is unary-index evaluation with accumulator $c$
initial work tape stores $u$ and work head is at $h$
replaced:
Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $r, u, p$ be binary words, and let the input be
$x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{pair}(1^k \mathbin{+\!\!+} r, u)$. Started in the
unary-index evaluation state with accumulator $c$, $|p|$ input bits consumed, work word
$u$, and work head $h$, the non-tautology verifier after exactly $2k$ steps is in the
same state with $|p| + 2k$ bits consumed and work head $h + k$.
